summary: The inclusive upper bound has at most 50 binary digits, so the complete legal domain is too tightly bounded for an honest fourfold runtime-scaling verdict in the governing bit-length variable.

workload_bound.source_constraint: n is from 1 through 10^15 inclusive, hence bit_length(n) is at most 50

replacement_checks.evidence: The accepted implementation computes L small depths, considers at most L possible set-bit counts, and scans exactly L bound bits for each qualifying count, performing at most L^2 combinatorial scan iterations with L <= 50.
Authored cases cover n=1 and n=10^15, every legal k from 0 through 5, both samples, power-of-two boundaries, inclusion of n itself, dense one-bit patterns, and unattainable depths.
